correctness.rationale: The repair's cyclic indices give cross-nonneighbor triples {j−4,j−3,j−2} modulo 7. In any induced subgraph with both bipartition classes nonempty, the stars of the selected odd vertices have simplex nerve and contractible intersections; their union and the even simplex are contractible, and the intersection is generated by the restricted nonneighbor triples. Reduced Mayer–Vietoris shifts the relevant homology by one. Each triangle has a unique endpoint edge and no larger face exists in the intersection, so H̃_t(Ind) vanishes for all t≥3. With one part empty the independence complex is a simplex. On W the intersection is the cycle on edges {6,10},{0,10},{0,2},{2,6}, giving H̃₂ of dimension 1 and β₅,₈≥1. For an even vertex pair at index distance d, each endpoint has d partner choices satisfying the required cross-nonadjacency, so 7(1²+2²+3²)=98; three selected even vertices would be consecutive, but their endpoint pair cannot be contained in a triple excluding the middle. Independent replay at /workspace/branches/d9ad2d97-bc9d-469b-9c4c-7ea1f2d545dc/independent_c14_check.py and full.log agrees: all 16,384 subsets over F₂ yield no homology ≥3 (UCT also gives the QQ upper bound), exact QQ witness ranks (7,13,2), and matching counts (98,0,0). Reviewed archived algorithms without running them. Banerjee–Nevo Theorem 1.1(ii) applies by bipartiteness; the induced two-edge restriction supports a degree-(2s+2) first syzygy of its s-th power. Neither argument fixes either power value.

value.rationale: This is the natural noncubic test case specified in the powers question, not an isolated selection just because enumeration is cheap. Its exact first-power value fixes the applicable bipartite powers upper line and the induced-matching census supplies the opposing line, leaving precisely two choices for each s≥2. The extremal cycle explains why the induced-matching bound alone misses even the first-power value. The repair provides a finite structural mechanism and does not claim to solve a general powers problem.
